messages:
maria: quick question — we don't have an explicit hot-swap policy for when the primary model is saturated, right? what's the current behavior?

owen: today requests queue and we spill to region fallback or lower-priority capacity. no automatic model-switching.

ravi: right. we've kept model variants separate because of KV cache / context compatibility concerns. switching mid-request is tricky.

sam: but customers keep asking for graceful degrade to cheaper/quantized variants when GPUs are pegged. can we do capacity-based failover to a smaller variant?

maria: sketch idea: when queue_length or GPU_util > X for Y seconds, route new requests for that route -> fallback_variant. keep original model for in-flight.

julie: must consider semantics: different variants may change output quality and token costs. also cache + prefix-caching invalidation. do we accept that for free tier only?

ravi: policy knobs we need: allowed_variants (same architecture family), max_delta_p95 (ms), per_tier_override, warmup_delay, telemetry_tagging. also an explicit "deny auto-fallback" flag per customer.

maria: example config proto I was thinking of:
```
fallback_policy:
  mode: auto
  triggers:
    - metric: queue_length
      threshold: 45
      window_s: 20
    - metric: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 220
      window_s: 30
  candidates:
    - model: rwd-13b-q4_1
      max_delta_p95: 50
    - model: rwd-7b-int8
      max_delta_p95: 150
  per_tier:
    free: allow
    standard: allow
    enterprise: require_explicit_ok
  sticky_duration_s: 300
  telemetry_label: "auto_variant_fallback"
```

ownen: sticky_duration is important — we should avoid flip-flopping every minute. also a cool-off that prefers the original model once capacity stabilizes.

sam: two enforcement modes: optimistic (route then monitor quality, revert if regression) vs conservative (only route to variants that pass eval thresholds). conservative is safer especially for SLAs.

julie: from console/UX POV, we need: per-route indicator (green/orange/red), timeline of fallback events, which variant served each request, and a quick toggle to opt-out. also alerting when enterprise traffic was served by fallback.

ravi: on telemetry: tag traces with fallback_reason and variant_id. export histogram of quality metrics vs baseline. add a regression alert if variant deviates beyond allowed thresholds for > N requests.

maria: ops question — should fallbacks be region-aware? e.g., we prefer a cheaper variant in the same region to avoid cross-region egress + latency.

owen: yes. routing top priority order: 1) same region same family 2) same region different family 3) cross-region fallback (last resort). always respect customer network policy.

sam: negotiations: enterprise customers will want a knob: disable auto-fallback entirely or only allow to verified variants. free tier might tolerate more aggressive switching.

julie: console mock: show a per-route toggle "Enable auto model fallback" with per-tier default and an audit log that surfaces who enabled it and why it triggered.

ravi: implementation notes: we can wire the failover decision into the router as a policy evaluation. evaluation inputs: route config, current signals (gpu_util, queue_len, p95), customer_tier, recent_fallbacks_count. decision outputs: route_to_model and telemetry labels.

maria: one more gotcha — KV cache compatibility. if variant has incompatible KV layout we must avoid switching (or accept cold-start hit and drop cache tag). add a compatibility bit in model catalog.

nowen: test plan: simulate saturation in staging by throttling capacity and ensure requests route to fallback variant, metrics are tagged, and console shows event. add chaos test to ensure sticky_duration behaves.

sam: can we also add an API for customers: GET /routes/:id/fallback-policy and POST to override per-customer? useful for sales/SEs.

julie: +1. include a read-only column in billing that shows tokens served by fallback vs tokens served by primary. customers will ask.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/auto-fallback-poc to staging started by ravi at 1790001180 :rocket:

maria: action items: (1) ravi spike schema and model catalog flag for compatibility, (2) owen wire policy eval in router, (3) julie prototype console indicators, (4) sam create API hooks + billing tag — aim for staging POC early next week.

ravi: will post a short doc with proposed proto and test scenarios later today.

sam: thanks — this covers most of the tradeoffs. we should also sync with runtime to understand quantized warmup penalty.

maria: ok closing here for now, ping me if you want to join the spike. :thumbsup:
